subject.title: Design: Telegram isolated ingress holds per-chat lane for the entire agent turn — long turns block the group, then die at 25 min

question: Should Telegram isolated ingress release the per-chat/topic spool lane after durable handoff to session admission instead of after the full agent turn completes?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but the permanent fix changes Telegram transport ordering, duplicate/replay safety, timeout semantics, and downstream session admission ownership, so maintainers need to choose the contract before automation edits code.

options.title: Detach After Durable Handoff
options.body: Move the Telegram spool lane lifetime to ingestion/classification plus durable session handoff, then let session admission own active-run ordering and steering.

options.title: Keep Lane Ownership And Narrow Mitigations
options.body: Preserve the current one-handler-per-lane model and tune timeout, progress, or error visibility while accepting that same-lane messages still cannot reach steering during a long turn.

options.title: Split Into Narrow Follow-Ups
options.body: Track handler-timeout visibility, collect starvation, and claude-cli queueMessage support separately while keeping this issue as the lane-ownership design decision.

recommendation.title: Detach After Durable Handoff
recommendation.body: Move the Telegram spool lane lifetime to ingestion/classification plus durable session handoff, then let session admission own active-run ordering and steering.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the current assignee and authored the related run-lifecycle work that frames the downstream session-admission contract.
